body.statement: For \(K=2\), \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), and \(\gamma_2,\delta_2\in[-1/8,1/8]\), \(P^{(2)}_{a,\gamma_2,\delta_2}\) is normalized, has uniform \(X\)- and \(W\)-margins, and every one of its eight cells is at least \((1-2^{-a_L})/16\). Its conditional-expectation operator sends \(s_2(W)\) to \(2^{-a}s_2(X)\), and \(b(x)=1/2+(\gamma_2+2^{-a}\delta_2)s_2(x)\). For \(0<c_{\rm link}<1<C_{\rm link}<\infty\) and \(0<\eta<1/2\), the law belongs to \(\mathcal P_2(a)\); the link inequalities have uniform multiplicative slack \(\min\{1-c_{\rm link},C_{\rm link}-1\}>0\), and each marginal balance inequality has additive slack at least \(1/4\).
body.justification: The smallest table displays operator attenuation, regression movement, and strict multinomial legality in the same observed law.
body.gap: Gaussian noisy-operator examples do not verify positivity and common-law coupling, while multinomial identity examples do not carry a conditional operator.
body.consumer: The instance is the algebraic unit test for the lower-bound perturbations and for split-statistic implementations at \(K=2\).
